hints: Focus on whether each named change mainly breaks bonds (needs energy in) or makes bonds (releases energy out).
Remember atomisation turns a substance into separate gaseous atoms, so bonds are broken and energy is absorbed.
Consider what is always made in neutralisation, $\text{H}^+ + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}$, and whether making that bond releases energy.
walkthrough:
**Recall what the sign means**

Think simply first. A positive $\Delta H$ means endothermic, energy is taken in. A negative $\Delta H$ means exothermic, energy is given out.

Rule to use:
$$\text{breaking bonds absorbs energy (+)}, \quad \text{making bonds releases energy (-)}$$

**Test atomisation, combustion and formation**

Atomisation is $\text{element} \rightarrow \text{gaseous atoms}$. Bonds are broken, so $\Delta H_{at}$ is always positive.

Combustion is burning in oxygen to make oxides like $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Strong new bonds are made, so $\Delta H_c$ is always negative. Formation from elements can be either, for example formation of $\text{CO}_2$ is negative but formation of $\text{NO}$ is positive.

**Confirm neutralisation**

Neutralisation of acid + base always includes:
$$\text{H}^+(aq) + \text{OH}^-(aq) \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$$
Making the O-H bond in water always releases energy, so $\Delta H_{neut}$ is always negative and exothermic.

options.A: Incorrect. Atomisation produces separate gaseous atoms, so covalent or metallic bonds must be broken. Bond breaking is endothermic, so enthalpy change of atomisation is always positive, not negative.
options.B: Incorrect. Combustion forms very stable products such as $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. A lot of energy is released when those strong bonds form, so enthalpy change of combustion is always negative (exothermic), not positive.
options.C: Incorrect. Formation can be exothermic or endothermic depending on the compound. For example, $\Delta H_f$ of $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is negative, but $\Delta H_f$ of $\text{NO}$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$ is positive.
options.D: Correct. Neutralisation always forms water from $\text{H}^+$ and $\text{OH}^-$. Bond formation releases energy, so the reaction is always exothermic and $\Delta H_{neut}$ is always negative, about $-57$ kJ mol-1 for strong acid plus strong base.
